title: Evaluation of the multilingual mobile app InterAPPtion for families with flight experience
summary: Children with flight experience often struggle with learning, language, or interacting with other children. This may be because they have experienced traumatic events, because their parents are very stressed themselves, or because they have had few opportunities to play, attend preschool or school and are more frequently exposed to screen time. The INCLUDE project offers these families low-threshold support. As part of the project, the “Parent’s College” (PaCo) program was developed: In small groups with interpreters, parents receive information about their children’s development. Results so far show that children who participated in the project demonstrate better learning performance in the short term—but this effect wears off after a few months. This study aims to investigate whether an app on parents’ smartphones can help sustain these positive effects for longer and improve children’s learning performance in the long term.
conditions: learning performance, PTSD symptoms, parental stress, behavioral problems, language and communication problems

interventions.name:
EG: App group (receives complete version of InterAPPtion)
T1 baseline assessment, T2 after 3 months, T3 after 6 months, T4 after 12 months

CG: Parents receive very basic version of app (only plain images and written explanations of the guidelines, with no additional animations, interactive features, or further instructions)
T1 baseline assessment, T2 after 3 months, T3 after 6 months, T4 after 12 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children with at least one parent or guardian with flight experience, living in branches of the Ankerzentrum Manching or in shared housing in Munich
Exclusion criteria:
previously diagnosed developmental disorder or illness in the child or the primary caregiver (e.g., intellectual disability, serious illness/developmental disorder, etc.) that prevents participation in the study.
